messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — gpu-serving/gpu-west-1 queue depth rising rapidly, autoscaler rejected scale request. root_ts=2250001234
Ashley: I'm on it. seeing queue go 220 -> 480 in ~8m. frontend 5xxs increasing. paging @Siddharth (overnight oncall).
Siddharth: ack. any obvious errors in autoscaler?
eng-runtime-bot: logs excerpt:
```
ERROR autoscaler: scale request rejected: quotaExceeded: requested 6 nodes, quota max 4 (project quota)
WARN runtime: avg_latency_per_token=78ms, in_flight=312, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.07
INFO batching: continuous_batching.params=changed_by=deploy/2026-03-14T22:07Z commit=ab1234
```
Louise: that commit is the batching tweak we rolled yesterday to lower batching latency (reduced max_batch_wait to 8ms and lowered prefix_cache_ttl). seems plausible.
Siddharth: kv cache hit rate at 7% is terrible — normal is ~70-80%. If prefix_cache_ttl got lowered to 30s from 5m we could be seeing high cache thrash + much higher latency per request -> more concurrent tokens -> hits pool cap.
Katie: CS-Ops report: 2 enterprise customers reported degraded API responses and increased request timeouts starting 22:40 UTC. They're seeing 502/504 from our hosted endpoints. Escalated to enterprise support.
Ashley: immediate mitigations? can we roll back batching change? also can we route heavy customers to dedicated pool or fallback model?
Louise: rollback looks safe. previous commit id before ab1234 is aa9876. Rolling back batching params should restore prefix_cache_ttl and batching windows. I can trigger a config rollback.
Sebastian: manual scale request to increase pool max will be blocked by cloud quota (we hit project GPU quota). We can request emergency quota increase but it's slow. Alternative: redirect some routes to smaller quantized model variant (q4f32 -> q4_0) to reduce per-token latency. That should reduce concurrency pressure.
Siddharth: steps I'll take now:
1) flip traffic route for non-SLA-dev traffic to model-variant-compact (q4_0) for gpu-west-1 (quick route rule)
2) ask Louise to rollback batching config (deploy rollback)
3) CS to notify impacted tenants and open support tickets
4) monitor kv cache hit rate and queue depth
Ashley's message: please annotate customer-impact in the incident doc and set severity to SEV2 for now.
CS-Ops: raising tickets and sending proactive email to affected accounts; logging impacted request_ids from 22:40-22:55.
Louise: running rollback command now:
```
# rollback batching config to commit aa9876
./deploy-tool rollback config batching --env=prod --to=aa9876 --reason="hotfix: revert continuous batching params"
```
eng-runtime-bot: rollback started, expected propagation ~45s. KV cache warming disabled flag was previously false, re-enabling TTL=5m.
Siddharth: routing change applied: `route:update gpu-west-1 /v1/generate -> model:compact` for non-dedicated keys. 
eng-runtime-bot: observed metrics after actions (22:50->22:58): queue depth peaked 485 -> 180, kv_cache_hit_rate climbing 7% -> 58%, avg_latency_per_token down 78ms -> 34ms. autoscaler still limited by quota but effective concurrency reduced.
Ashley: good. any residual 5xxs?
CS-Ops: 5xx rate dropped to baseline for most tenants; two enterprise customers still seeing intermittent 504s — support tickets created and escalated to accounts team.
Sebastian: follow-ups: (a) remove the low ttl change from future batching PRs, (b) add autoscaler defensive behavior to not request >project quota (graceful degrade earlier), (c) add a canary gating test for prefix_cache hit rate when modifying batching params.
Siddharth: leaving detailed mitigation notes in incident doc and will hand over overnight to Sebastian (next oncall). Ashley - handing off to Sebastian at 23:00 UTC.
Sebastian: acked. I will keep watch and try to request emergency quota increase first thing tomorrow. Also will run a canary against a single shard for any batching param changes.
Ashley: thanks team. incident severity downgrade to SEV3 23:05 after stable metrics. Final note: root cause tied to batching config regression (reduced prefix_cache_ttl + lower wait window) which increased cold-kv misses -> amplified per-request token latency -> queue growth -> hit autoscaler/project quota -> throttling. Postmortem owners: Louise (rollback/owners), Sebastian (autoscaler / quota mitigations), Siddharth (routing/fallback patterns), Katie (customer comms).
CS-Ops: all impacted customers notified, follow-ups scheduled.
incidents-bot: incident classified as "partial outage". thread archived to incidents log 2250001234 at 2250003600. :white_check_mark:"
